title: Catching a yawn: A multimodal experimental protocol for investigating sleepiness under visual and auditory yawning stimuli featuring human and digital characters
author: Liang, Khotchasing, et al.

steps.title: Randomize conditions and set up monitoring
steps.instruction: Randomize the order of the two yawning stimulus conditions (with sound and without sound) in a counterbalanced fashion. Ensure the participant is alone in the experimental room while the experimenter monitors the session remotely via a live physiological data feed and video stream.

substeps.instruction: Randomize and counterbalance the two conditions.
Confirm participant is alone in the room.
Set up remote monitoring of physiological signals and video.

steps.title: Start physiological recording and give instructions
steps.instruction: At the beginning of each condition, start continuous physiological recording and instruct the participant to watch the videos naturally, maintaining a comfortable and relaxed posture. No specific yawning instructions are given.

steps.title: Present yawning stimulus
steps.instruction: Present the stimulus sequence for approximately 5 minutes, consisting of about 50 discrete yawning events each lasting roughly 6 seconds. Continue recording all physiological signals and video. Monitor for signs of sleep onset (e.g., sustained eye closure); if sleep onset occurs, note the timestamp and keep recording uninterrupted.

substeps.instruction: Play stimulus (~5 min, ~50 yawns, ~6 s each).
Record physiological data and video continuously.
Watch for sleep onset; log timestamp if observed.

steps.title: Conduct post‑stimulus assessment
steps.instruction: After stimulus presentation, stop the video and assess subjective sleepiness using the Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (KSS). Have the participant complete a brief questionnaire about yawning behavior, indicating whether they yawned or felt an urge to yawn.

steps.title: Implement wakefulness reset
steps.instruction: Following the first condition, conduct a wakefulness reset lasting about 15 minutes. Increase laboratory lighting, encourage light activities such as standing, brief walking, or casual movement, and avoid intentional or exaggerated upper‑body stretching. Light conversation may be used if needed. At the end of the reset, reassess sleepiness with the KSS. If the participant remains drowsy, extend the reset or add additional light activities before proceeding.

substeps.instruction: Encourage light activities (standing, walking, casual movement).
If still drowsy, extend reset or add activities.

steps.title: Repeat procedure for second condition
steps.instruction: Carry out the same sequence—start recording, present stimulus, monitor, conduct post‑stimulus KSS and yawning questionnaire—for the second yawning stimulus condition.

steps.title: Remove equipment
steps.instruction: After both conditions have been completed, remove all physiological sensing equipment from the participant.
